saml.description: Vault session tokens are bearer credentials and can be reused across multiple API calls until expiry or revocation.
saml.source: Vault token lookup-self API; token auth method docs
saml.note: Do not flag repeated use of the same valid Vault token as replay when token_num_uses is unlimited.

saml.description: If a platform does not enforce JWT nbf, that is spec-compliant because nbf is optional.
saml.note: Do not flag acceptance of tokens without nbf or with future nbf solely on that basis.

saml.description: Lookup-style artifacts and self-inspection endpoints are idempotent unless explicitly documented as single-use.
saml.note: Repeated self-lookups are not replay vulnerabilities.

saml.description: Vault token_num_uses value 0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses.
saml.source: Vault token and SAML role read APIs
saml.note: Do not interpret num_uses=0 as an exhausted or one-time token.

saml.description: Policy and auth-role updates take effect immediately for associated users and tokens.
saml.source: Vault /sys/policy docs: updated policy takes effect immediately to all associated users
saml.note: A changed authorization result after an admin update is by design, not a flow-coherence bug.

saml.description: SAML response and assertion signature validation are opt-in and default to false.
saml.source: Vault SAML auth method config docs
saml.note: Acceptance under this default configuration is an insecure-default check; do not misclassify it as bypassing an explicitly enabled validation control.

saml.description: When an admin updates SAML auth configuration such as IdP metadata URL, IdP certificate, or issuer-related settings, subsequent logins are evaluated under the new trust configuration.
saml.note: Acceptance after an admin-authorized trust change is by design, not trust-anchor substitution.

saml.description: Vault token lookup-self display_name may include the auth mount path as a prefix before the upstream identity value.
saml.note: A prefixed display_name like mount-user is normal and should not be treated as identity confusion.

saml.constraint: SAML login in Vault is a 3-step flow: POST /v1/auth/{mount}/sso_service_url to obtain RelayState and token_poll_id, POST the forged SAMLResponse to /v1/auth/{mount}/callback, then POST /v1/auth/{mount}/token with client_verifier and token_poll_id to obtain the Vault token. The fuzzer MUST preserve the same flow state across these steps; testing /callback alone is not a complete login oracle.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution default-config testing, create the SAML config without setting validate_response_signature=true or validate_assertion_signature=true. Both settings default to false, so acceptance under that configuration is an insecure default test, not a misconfiguration artifact.

For I1 assertion integrity tests, Vault exposes two independent signature-validation toggles: validate_response_signature and validate_assertion_signature. To test unsigned-assertion or spurious-signature acceptance correctly, the fuzzer MUST vary these explicitly and interpret results accordingly; enabling only response validation does not imply assertion validation.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, idp_entity_id is only required when idp_metadata_url is not set. If configuration uses idp_metadata_url, issuer trust may come from metadata instead. To test skipped issuer validation, configure without metadata URL and omit or vary idp_entity_id as documented; otherwise the test may exercise metadata-derived issuer checks instead of the intended path.

bound_subjects matching semantics are controlled by bound_subjects_type. If bound_subjects_type=string, matching is exact string only; wildcards like * are literal characters. If bound_subjects_type=glob, * wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity tests, the fuzzer MUST either omit bound_subjects entirely or set bound_subjects_type=glob with an intentional pattern; do NOT set bound_subjects='*' under string mode.

bound_attributes matching semantics are controlled by bound_attributes_type. If bound_attributes_type=string (default), attribute values must match exactly; wildcard characters are literal. If bound_attributes_type=glob, * wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity tests requiring multiple attribute values to pass one role, the fuzzer MUST omit the exact-match attribute constraint or switch to glob mode intentionally; do NOT assume '*' works under the default string mode.

bound_attributes accepts string values or comma-separated lists of strings and authenticates if the SAML attribute matches at least one expected value. For I5 tests, this is string-list membership semantics, not numeric typing. Do not interpret acceptance across comma-separated values as overbroad authorization unless the matched value was outside the configured set.

token_num_uses=0 is a sentinel meaning unlimited uses, not zero uses. Never treat 0 as 'single-use disabled by exhaustion'. For session-use-budget tests, any positive token_num_uses counts every API call made with the token, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret.

If token_num_uses limits the issued Vault token, verification calls consume uses before the protected-resource read. Because the fuzzer commonly performs verify_granted_identity and then verify_read_secret, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2 for one inspect plus one access call, and 3 if an additional entity lookup is performed.

KV v2 max_versions uses 0 as a sentinel for the platform default of 10 versions, not literal zero versions. delete_version_after uses '0s' as a sentinel meaning no automatic deletion timer. Never assume 0 disables storage or causes immediate deletion.

For KV v2 CAS tests, options.cas=0 means write only if the key does not yet exist; it is not a generic 'disable CAS' value. If cas_required is enabled, omitting cas is invalid, and writing to a soft-deleted key still requires cas to match the current version.

For I5 access tests on KV v2, list capability is checked on /metadata/ paths while read capability is checked on /data/ paths. The fuzzer MUST seed and verify reads against /v1/{engine}/data/{path}; using metadata/list endpoints tests a different permission surface and can produce false positives.

Vault policy updates take effect immediately for associated users and tokens. For I3 config-change sequences, a changed outcome after an admin updates policy or role configuration is BY DESIGN unless the same request is evaluated inconsistently without an intervening authorized config change.

Vault identity group aliases map external group names from the SAML groups_attribute into internal identity groups. For I5 group-policy-escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST create the internal group, obtain the auth mount accessor, and create the group alias with the exact external group name emitted in the SAML assertion; otherwise missing policy inheritance is a setup failure, not a security result.

Vault allows external identities to be bound through aliases, and alias-name cardinality is security-sensitive. Reusing the same alias name on the same mount can collapse privileges across entities. For I4 collision tests, the fuzzer SHOULD intentionally vary alias names and mount accessors and treat alias reuse as a documented risk surface, not as accidental platform normalization.

For MFA-bypass-via-binding-rule tests, login enforcement creation requires mfa_method_ids plus at least one scope selector among auth_method_accessors, auth_method_types, identity_group_ids, or identity_entity_ids. A login enforcement missing all selectors is invalid setup and cannot be used as an MFA oracle.

SAML signature validation is opt-in in Vault SAML config: validate_response_signature defaults to false and validate_assertion_signature defaults to false. For I1 signature-integrity tests, explicitly control these flags. To test insecure defaults, leave both unset/false; to test hardened behavior, set both true. Do not assume Vault validates either response or assertion signatures by default.

idp_entity_id is required only when idp_metadata_url is not set. If idp_metadata_url is used and no explicit issuer binding is configured, issuer trust comes from metadata. For the saml_issuer_mismatch default-config test, omission of explicit issuer binding can make issuer validation depend entirely on metadata-derived trust; do not assume a separate issuer check exists unless configured.

SAML login is a 3-step flow in Vault: obtain SSO service URL -> POST SAMLResponse to /auth/{mount}/callback -> exchange token_poll_id + client_verifier at /auth/{mount}/token. I3 tests must keep token_poll_id, client_verifier/client_challenge, RelayState, and callback/token exchange in the SAME flow instance. Mixing artifacts across flows will fail for flow reasons, not security reasons.

The ACS callback alone does not return the Vault bearer token. The usable session credential is only returned by POST /auth/{mount}/token. The fuzzer must not treat callback success as authenticated session success.

client_challenge must be the base64-encoded SHA-256 digest of the later client_verifier, and must be at least 44 bytes. For any SAML login test, the executor must generate a matching verifier/challenge pair; otherwise token exchange failure is a setup error, not a security rejection.

bound_attributes matching semantics are controlled by bound_attributes_type. Default is string, which requires exact string matching; glob enables * wildcard matching. For I4 multi-identity tests requiring multiple different attribute values to pass the same role, omit the exact-match attribute constraint or explicitly use glob mode. Do NOT use wildcard-looking values under default string mode; they are treated as literals.

bound_attributes values are documented as a single string or comma-separated list of strings. Vault docs do not specify non-string cross-type coercion for SAML attribute matching. For I5 type-confusion testing, treat bound_attributes as string-oriented matching and separately probe whether non-string SAML attribute encodings are coerced or rejected; do not assume numeric/boolean coercion is supported.

token_num_uses uses sentinel 0 = unlimited uses, not literal zero uses. Any positive token_num_uses counts EVERY API call made with that session, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the sequence performs both self-lookup and secret-read, minimum safe value is 2; if entity lookup is also performed, minimum safe value is 3 or more depending on verification steps.
saml.source: auth/saml role read response; token lookup-self semantics

saml.constraint: Vault token TTL-related fields use sentinel 0 values that do not mean immediate expiry: token_ttl=0, token_max_ttl=0, token_explicit_max_ttl=0, and token_period=0 indicate unset/default/no explicit limit semantics rather than literal zero-second lifetime. Never interpret 0 as 'expired now' or 'disabled underlying check' for these fields.

KV v2 read paths require /data/ in the URL, while KV v1 reads do not. The extracted verify_read_secret uses KV v1 /v1/{engine}/{path} because the docs include both KV versions and no mount version is fixed by SAML docs. The fuzzer must align seed/read operations to the actual mounted KV version or access tests will fail with 404 for the wrong reason.

Vault group aliases for external groups require mount_accessor and canonical_id. For SAML group-to-policy tests, create an external identity group and map the SAML groups_attribute values via group aliases; simply setting member_entity_ids on a group is not equivalent to external group alias mapping.

External identity behavior can be namespace-sensitive for group policy application. By default, group_policy_application_mode is within_namespace_hierarchy; only when set to any do group policies apply regardless of namespace hierarchy. For I5 group policy escalation tests in Enterprise/multi-namespace setups, control this global mode or namespace effects may look like authorization bugs.

For I2 SAML expiry tests such as expired_assertion, include a control login through the same SAML flow without the expiry mutation first. Otherwise a failed attack login cannot be distinguished from broken SAML setup, bad RelayState, or mismatched verifier/challenge artifacts.

Admin-authorized config changes to SAML trust settings are immediate by design. For I3 config-change tests, a valid test must show the SAME kind of request being evaluated differently before vs after the change under controlled conditions; do not flag acceptance under the new admin-configured trust anchor as a vulnerability by itself.

SAML config trust source is mutually exclusive: configure_jwt_validation MUST set either idp_metadata_url OR the manual trio idp_sso_url + idp_entity_id + idp_cert. Do not send idp_metadata_url together with manual IdP fields or setup will be invalid.

Vault SAML signature validation defaults are insecure for testing: validate_response_signature defaults to false and validate_assertion_signature defaults to false. For secure-baseline tests, explicitly set both to true. For the insecure-default attack pattern saml_cert_substitution, create the provider with both left false; acceptance is testing the documented default, not a misconfiguration in the fuzzer.

Issuer validation can be skipped by configuration: if idp_metadata_url is used, issuer comes from metadata; if manual config is used, idp_entity_id is required. For saml_issuer_mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST ensure the configured trust anchor includes the expected IdP entity ID. A default-config test that omits issuer binding is only valid when using metadata-driven trust or when intentionally testing missing issuer binding behavior.

SAML login is a 3-step flow in Vault, not a single token-returning ACS callback. The fuzzer MUST perform: obtain SSO service URL -> POST forged SAMLResponse to /callback -> exchange token_poll_id + client_verifier at /token. Treating /callback as the final login result will misclassify flow failures and break I3 session binding tests.

The ACS URL used at login MUST exactly match one of the configured acs_urls. The sso_service_url request's acs_url is validated against configured acs_urls, so the fuzzer must keep setup and login ACS values coherent.

The SAML token exchange is PKCE-like and session-bound: client_challenge must be the base64-encoded SHA-256 digest of the later client_verifier, and token_poll_id comes from the same SSO initiation. For I3 flow-coherence tests, do not mix token_poll_id or verifier values across flows; Vault binds them.
saml.source: auth/saml obtain SSO service URL and obtain vault token

saml.constraint: bound_attributes values are documented as single strings or comma-separated lists of strings. For I5 claim/attribute type-coercion tests, Vault SAML docs do not specify non-string cross-type behavior. The fuzzer should test numeric coercion explicitly by binding a numeric-looking string value and sending alternate typed representations in the assertion, but must expect undocumented behavior rather than guaranteed coercion support.

token_num_uses value 0 is a sentinel meaning unlimited uses, not literal zero uses. Never interpret 0 as 'single-use disabled by exhaustion'. If token_num_uses is set to a positive value, every authenticated API call consumes a use, including verify_granted_identity before verify_read_secret. Minimum safe value for sequences that do both is 2; use 3+ if additional session-inspection calls are present.
saml.source: auth/saml read role; token lookup-self semantics

saml.constraint: Vault token and TTL numeric sentinels: token_ttl=0, token_max_ttl=0, token_explicit_max_ttl=0, and token_period=0 in role reads indicate default/unset behavior rather than literal immediate expiry. Do not assume zero means expired or disabled. Configure explicit nonzero values when testing freshness boundaries.

For I2 SAML expiry tests such as saml_expired_assertion, include a control login through the same configured role and flow first. A failed expired assertion without a successful control cannot distinguish assertion-time enforcement from broken SAML setup.

Vault identity group aliases for SAML groups require the auth mount accessor. The fuzzer MUST call get_mount_accessor and use the accessor for the same SAML mount when creating group aliases; using the wrong mount accessor will silently bind external groups to the wrong auth source and invalidate I4/I5 group tests.

External identity groups are intended to represent external memberships via aliases. For SAML group-mapping tests, prefer type='external' groups plus create_group_alias rather than manually populating member_entity_ids, or the test may not reflect real external-group resolution behavior.

Entity alias names are security-sensitive and can be reused across entities. Vault docs explicitly warn that multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias and gain its privileges. For I4 collision tests, alias cardinality is a real attack surface, not a false positive; the fuzzer should preserve exact alias names and cross-check entity IDs carefully.

Entity merges are administrative and by design. For I4 collision testing, do not use /identity/entity/merge or any admin alias reassignment during the same scenario, or distinct principals may collapse due to explicit admin action rather than broker confusion.

KV v2 pathing matters: verify_read_secret and seed_protected_resource MUST use /v1/{engine}/data/{path}, not /v1/{engine}/{path}. Using the v1-style path against a KV v2 mount returns the wrong result and causes false I5 failures.

KV v2 engine config sentinels: max_versions=0 means use Vault's default retention of 10 versions, not keep zero versions; delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic timed deletion, not immediate deletion. Never assume these sentinel values disable reads by expiring data instantly.

Vault policy updates take effect immediately for associated users by design. For I3 config-change tests, a new login evaluated under updated policy or role config is expected behavior. A valid coherence test must show inconsistent handling of the same logical request without relying on an admin-authorized policy change as the oracle.

Admin-authorized trust-anchor changes are by design in Vault SAML. If an admin updates IdP metadata URL, certificate, entity ID, or signature-validation flags, subsequent logins being evaluated under the new trust settings is expected. Do not flag acceptance under the new config as I1/I3 unless stale old trust remains accepted contrary to the updated configuration.
